notation.meaning: Variance of the group means: between-group part
Error variance, errors, regressors and identity matrix in the econometrics application
Average of $Y$ for a given value of $X$

blocks.md: The law of total variance splits how spread out an outcome is into two sources: spread within groups, and spread between the group averages. Wages vary partly because people with the same education earn different amounts, and partly because average wages differ across education levels. The total variance is exactly the average of the within-group variances plus the variance of the group averages.

blocks.title: Why it matters
blocks.md: It is the basis for saying how much inequality is between groups versus within them, and for the R-squared of a regression on group dummies.
Total variance = average variance within groups + variance of the group means.
Write $\mathrm{Var}(Y) = E[Y^2] - (E[Y])^2$, use the [Law of Iterated Expectations](note:law-of-iterated-expectations) on each term, and add and subtract $E\big[(E[Y\mid X])^2\big]$:

blocks.tex: E[Y^2] = E\big[E[Y^2\mid X]\big] = E\big[\mathrm{Var}(Y\mid X) + (E[Y\mid X])^2\big]

| Econometrics | $R^2$ from a regression on group dummies = between-group share |
